facts.text: Wyandotte was founded as a village of Ecorse Township in 1854 and became an incorporated city on December 12, 1866.
The city’s name honors the Wyandot people who lived nearby, a tribute made by early settlers who named their estate after the tribe.
In the 1920s, Wyandotte’s All Metal Products Company turned the town into a toy‑making hub, crafting metal airplanes and cars.
Every summer the Heritage Event Series celebrates local culture, while the second‑largest street‑art fair in Michigan draws artists from across the state.
The Wyandot tribe first arrived from Ontario, Canada, when French allies founded Detroit, establishing a peaceful trade relationship with early settlers.
